passage:
A school found its original bell in storage. Before electric bells, a worker had rung it by hand.
The principal placed it near the entrance with a sign explaining its history. Students tried to imagine school life when every sound depended on a person pulling a rope.
The bell made them think about invisible labor. Today, schedules happened automatically. In the past, someone had to make time audible.
During the school anniversary, the oldest teacher rang the bell once.
Its sound was rougher than the modern bell, but people listened closely. It reminded them that institutions are built not only by rules, but by repeated human actions.
